text: Without CI/CD, a mistake in a dbt model reaches production the same way a correct one does -- by someone running dbt run against prod and finding out afterward. This lesson adds the GitHub Actions workflow that tests every change to driftwood-analytics-platform before it can.

On every pull request touching the dbt project, this workflow checks out the repo, installs dbt, and runs dbt build -- models and tests together, in dependency order -- against Driftwood's Snowflake account using CI credentials, never production ones.
A real GitHub Actions run looks exactly like this -- one pass or fail signal per pull request, the same workflow-run summary Driftwood's CI produces.

The crucial detail is target ci, pointing this run at a schema that exists only for CI, built and torn down fresh each time -- never the prod schema Airflow writes to. A bad model can run, fail its tests, even fail loudly, without ever touching the dashboard leadership reads from.
dbt's own official CI diagram shows the same shape: pull requests building into a temporary staging schema, never the always-on production database.

state colon modified plus is what makes this practical at Driftwood's actual size -- it runs only the models that changed, plus everything downstream of them, not the whole project on every single pull request.
That state comparison is real, documented dbt Cloud behavior -- deferring to a prior manifest so only what actually changed gets rebuilt and retested.
Next lesson: provisioning the Snowflake infrastructure itself with Terraform, instead of clicking it together by hand.
